title: Package, build variant and delivery format
procedure: Confirm package(s), debug/release/staging/production variant and APK/AAB/split/Play delivery. Bind evidence to the uploaded hash; do not infer release from a filename.

title: Test accounts, banking data and OTP mechanism
procedure: Document role-separated test accounts and approved test bank accounts/cards; establish a test OTP mechanism. Keep credential values in the secret store.

title: Backend host and endpoint authorization
procedure: Review discovered hosts and endpoint ownership, exclusions and environment before active testing. Discovery is not permission to attack unrelated hosts.

title: Rooted-device and bypass authorization
procedure: Record explicit permission before extracting private storage or bypassing root/integrity controls. Record which device and techniques are approved.

title: Compliance and testing profile
procedure: Select the applicable regulator, PCI requirements and MAS testing profile. MASVS v2 controls do not contain the older L1/L2 verification levels.

title: Device, proxy and analysis tool readiness
procedure: Record selected serial, OS/ABI, tool versions and proxy visibility. Installed executables are not proof that their adapters ran.

title: DEX, resources and framework-specific code inventory
procedure: Inspect DEX/resources with JADX/Apktool and route Dart AOT, JS/Hermes, .NET and native binaries to matching tools. Decompiling the wrapper does not recover all business logic.

title: Framework, runtime and compilation mode
procedure: Identify JVM/Kotlin/Compose, Flutter, React Native/Hermes, Cordova/Capacitor, .NET/MAUI/Xamarin, Unity and native-library signals. Record engine version as unknown unless verified.

title: Manifest components, permissions and SDK levels
procedure: Inspect declared and effective manifest values, SDK-dependent defaults, exported components and permission guards.

title: Bundled resources and debug snapshots
procedure: Inventory Flutter assets/kernel snapshots, JavaScript bundles/maps, .NET assemblies and native libraries; absence of known names is inconclusive.

title: SDK and dependency inventory
procedure: Identify analytics, payments, crash SDKs and package versions from an SBOM or verified metadata. A marker alone does not identify a vulnerable version.

title: Signing certificate and build flags
procedure: Verify APK signature schemes v1 (JAR), v2, v3 (key rotation) and v4 with apksigner; confirm a production release certificate (not debug/test-keys) and that v2/v3 are enabled to block Janus-style DEX prepending. Presence of META-INF entries is not signature verification.

title: Baseline scanner analysis
procedure: Run or import hash-bound MobSF results; retain scanner versions and raw output. Treat scanner alerts as candidates.

title: Recover application code with the matching toolchain
procedure: Use JADX for DEX, Dart AOT tooling for Flutter, JS/Hermes tools for React Native, assembly tools for .NET, and native disassemblers for ELF. Record unsupported versions.

title: Embedded secrets, internal URLs and keys
procedure: Inspect strings and recovered code for credentials, keys and URLs. Classify public identifiers/placeholders separately; prove sensitive use without reading unnecessary data.

title: Trust and pinning implementation review
procedure: Trace active HTTP clients and trust callbacks in every code layer. String references to pinning APIs do not prove enforcement or bypassability.

title: Vulnerable package/version applicability
procedure: Compare verified versions with ecosystem advisories (Maven, pub.dev, npm, NuGet and native dependencies); confirm reachable affected code.

title: Storage implementation and key protection
procedure: Trace secure-storage and preference/database implementation in the actual library version. A package name does not prove Keystore-backed protection.

title: Native bridges and platform channel code
procedure: Review MethodChannel/EventChannel, React Native bridges, WebView JS interfaces, Cordova plugins, JNI and managed/native boundaries for validation and authorization.

title: Debug artifacts in the distributed build
procedure: Inspect debug snapshots, source maps, test metadata and development entry points; verify intended release variant before treating artifacts as findings.

title: Obfuscation and symbol protection
procedure: Inspect R8/ProGuard mappings, Dart --obfuscate/--split-debug-info, JS/Hermes and native/managed symbol configuration. Recoverability alone cannot prove build flags.

title: Instrumentation reaches the actual application layer
procedure: Confirm observer capabilities in JVM, Dart/native, JS/Hermes, managed and WebView layers; report partial visibility and missed startup/secondary processes.

title: Runtime API surface capture
procedure: Enumerate the app's runtime endpoints EXHAUSTIVELY in two authentication states. BEFORE login: launch the app and run mobile_discover_runtime_apis + mobile_traffic_history to capture startup/login-screen requests (unauthenticated surface). Log in reliably (verify the authenticated screen via mobile_ui_dump; retry on failure), then AFTER login drive every major flow and re-capture (authenticated surface). Merge both with the statically extracted URLs into one endpoint inventory tagged by source and auth-state; run mobile_api_harvest to normalize the captured traffic into deduped, parameterized endpoints (object ids collapsed to {id}) with their params and auth requirement in the inventory, and mobile_api_graph to map objects and producer->consumer id dependencies (endpoints that consume externally-produced ids are prime BOLA targets). If an OpenAPI/Swagger spec is recovered (api-docs/swagger.json in the app or backend), run mobile_openapi_ingest to add the documented (inferred) endpoints and diff them against the observed inventory — documented-but-unobserved endpoints to exercise, observed-but-undocumented ones are shadow APIs. The static inventory lists host-less endpoint PATH templates (from Retrofit/OkHttp code) separately from base URLs; the app often resolves a DIFFERENT base URL at runtime, so take the base URL seen in proxy traffic as authoritative, JOIN the static path templates to it, and actively trigger (drive the app / replay) any path that never appears in traffic (code-declared but unobserved = shadow/untested). Run mobile_api_model to infer parameter and response TYPES, the API version and a discovery confidence per endpoint, and mobile_coverage to see which checks have run on each endpoint and which remain untested. This feeds the OWASP/business-logic testing phases. Mark blocked (not failed) when the device lacks root.

title: Approved framework-specific repackaging or hooking
procedure: If approved, preserve the original hash, tool version and patch recipe. Flutter engine compatibility varies; never assume Reflutter restores source or enables JIT on every release.

title: Native TLS interception setup
procedure: Choose an engine-compatible, approved technique for native/Dart TLS. Record whether interception succeeded and which validation behavior the patch changed.

title: Client-specific proxy and trust behavior
procedure: Identify Dio/http, OkHttp, Cronet, WebView and native clients actually used. JVM hooks and OS proxy settings may miss custom/native stacks.

title: Traffic visibility and coverage baseline
procedure: Capture one documented interaction and reconcile proxy/packet traffic with observer events. No events and failed interception are limitations, never security passes.

title: Pinning implementation and strength
procedure: Compare normal and controlled intercepted connections to verify certificate/public-key pinning; include rotation and backup pins.

title: Pinning bypass resistance
procedure: Compare approved hook, engine patch, controlled CA and proxy techniques against a baseline. Record each outcome and modified artifact hash.

title: Cleartext policy and actual transmission
procedure: Correlate manifest/network-security configuration with wire evidence. HTTP literals or client calls alone do not prove sensitive data exposure.

title: Backend TLS versions and ciphers
procedure: Probe approved hosts with a bounded TLS scanner; retain handshake evidence for each protocol/cipher conclusion.

title: Certificate chain, hostname and expiry validation
procedure: Use controlled self-signed, wrong-host and expired certificates. Distinguish pinning-related inspection limits from certificate validation results.

title: Sensitive fields and data minimization
procedure: Inspect approved test traffic for PAN/CVV/PII and unnecessary fields. TLS and any additional field encryption must be evaluated against the threat model; lack of field encryption alone is not a vulnerability.

title: Reachable deprecated API versions
procedure: Compare documented versions with observed routes and approved deployment scope; validate exposure and authorization on legacy versions.

title: Object and function authorization, BOLA/BFLA
procedure: Use two controlled owners and role-separated accounts; compare authorized/unauthorized responses and server-side effects on seeded objects. Register the owners/roles with mobile_identity_set, then run mobile_authz_sweep (or mobile_authz_diff for a single case) to decide each deterministically: it replays the owner's request as every other identity and unauthenticated and flags only actual disclosure or mutation, never a bare 2xx. Declare legitimately-shared/admin-accessible endpoints with mobile_authz_expect so expected access is not reported. Confirmed results auto-file as findings.

title: Cross-audience token acceptance and legacy API-family coverage
procedure: Enumerate every login/token-minting path the app or backend exposes (app login, convergent/third-party, SSO, account-link) and every API version family in the endpoint inventory (legacy v1/basic-token AND v2/JWT), not just the routes the app itself calls. Mint a token from EACH login path and replay it across v1 and v2 of every state-changing and read endpoint — especially payment/transfer/QR routes. A token minted for one audience/channel accepted on another (e.g. a CONVERGENT or third-party token on a fund-transfer or QR-payment route) is a critical authorization-boundary bypass. Record coverage for every enumerated endpoint family at least once; never conclude token-bound means safe from same-audience A-vs-B swaps alone.

title: Injection, mass assignment and excessive data
procedure: Use documented schemas and seeded objects for bounded validation tests; verify actual impact rather than treating reflected input as injection. Run mobile_schema_fuzz on a captured JSON request to mutate each field against its type (wrong type, null, removal, oversized) and flag 5xx server errors (input reaching an unhandled path); a clean 4xx is correct rejection. Run mobile_mass_assignment on create/update requests to inject privilege fields the request omitted (role, is_admin, verified, balance, status); a finding only when the response shows the injected value was applied. Run mobile_inject_probe on request parameters to confirm SSTI (evaluated-expression product in the response) and error-based SQLi (leaked DB error signature) — confirmed by evidence, not status. Run mobile_data_exposure to scan responses for sensitive fields/values a client should not receive (secrets, full PANs, SSNs, JWTs, keys). Run mobile_misconfig_probe to check CORS (reflected/credentialed arbitrary Origin) and missing security headers. For GraphQL endpoints, run mobile_graphql_probe to confirm schema introspection is enabled in production. These tools handle JSON and form-urlencoded bodies.

title: Rate and abuse controls
procedure: Agree on test thresholds and lockout recovery; record the permitted request rate and observed enforcement without stressing production.

title: Login abuse, lockout and CAPTCHA
procedure: Use approved test users and bounded attempts; verify lockout/CAPTCHA server enforcement and recovery.

title: PIN/MPIN enrollment and verification
procedure: Verify enrollment, retry limits and where the decision is enforced. Test a seeded PIN workflow without exposing real customer credentials.

title: Biometric authentication and key binding
procedure: Verify BiometricPrompt/CryptoObject and Keystore authorization requirements. Observing an API invocation does not prove protection against boolean bypass.

title: OTP validity, reuse and retry controls
procedure: Use the approved test OTP mechanism for expiry, replay, bounded retries and transaction binding; assess SMS leakage separately. Run mobile_ratelimit_probe against the OTP-verify (and login/reset) request to confirm the server throttles/locks out brute force; no throttle across many attempts is a finding.

title: Token storage, expiry, rotation and logout
procedure: Compare storage and replay behavior before/after expiry, refresh, logout and account switch using test sessions. If sessions use JWTs, run mobile_jwt_probe: it decodes the token (alg:none, missing/expired/over-long exp, HS/RS confusion) and actively replays an alg:none and a tampered-signature variant — a forged token accepted while the genuine one is accepted confirms a signature-verification bypass (auto-filed critical). After logging out (or rotating the token), run mobile_session_probe on a pre-logout authenticated request to confirm the old token is actually invalidated server-side; a still-valid token is a session-management finding.

title: Session fixation and concurrent devices
procedure: Record session identities before/after login and test approved concurrent-session policy on separate test devices.

title: Password/MPIN and account recovery
procedure: Exercise seeded recovery flows; verify identity binding, token expiry, reuse and invalidation.

title: Step-up authentication for high-risk actions
procedure: Verify transfers, beneficiaries and limit changes require the documented fresh authorization on the server, including replay and stale-session cases. Use mobile_txn_probe to test transaction-limit bypass deterministically (amount over the configured max_amount) — a finding only when the server accepts it. Model the multi-step flow with mobile_workflow_set (ordered states + correlation field), drive a step out of order (replay a later step without its prerequisite), then mobile_workflow_check to confirm whether the server accepted the skipped-prerequisite transition.

title: Actual secure storage and Keystore backing
procedure: Trace the selected secure-storage implementation/version and key lifecycle. EncryptedSharedPreferences is not the only valid secure design.

title: Private app files, preferences, databases and caches
procedure: Inspect only the selected package's seeded test data with approved privilege. Record path, permissions and redacted evidence without exporting unrelated data.

title: Sensitive values persisted locally
procedure: Search seeded account numbers, balances, tokens, PIN-related data, statements and KYC artifacts; distinguish sensitive content from identifiers.

title: Database encryption and key separation
procedure: Inspect actual database bytes and key location; a SQLite/SQLCipher reference alone proves neither encryption nor exposure.

title: Sensitive data in runtime logs
procedure: Exercise sensitive test flows and correlate PID-filtered logs. Report redacted patterns and validate actual sensitivity.

title: Screenshots and task-switcher privacy
procedure: Inspect FLAG_SECURE on visited sensitive screens and test actual screenshots/recents behavior on supported OS versions.

title: Clipboard exposure and clearing
procedure: Observe clipboard API use and test seeded OTP/account-field copy/clear behavior; never capture clipboard contents from unrelated apps.

title: Keyboard, autofill and sensitive fields
procedure: Inspect password/PIN input settings and verify keyboard learning/autofill behavior. Widget flags alone do not cover custom Flutter/JS-rendered inputs.

title: Crash, ANR and analytics data leakage
procedure: Review controlled crash/ANR telemetry and analytics payloads using seeded values; avoid collecting real customer data.

title: Sensitive backup and device-transfer behavior
procedure: Test inclusion/exclusion rules and actual seeded data on supported Android versions. allowBackup=false is not universal proof against device-to-device transfers.

title: Crypto libraries and actual algorithms
procedure: Inventory JVM, Dart, JS, managed and native crypto; correlate references with runtime use and protected data.

title: Hardcoded keys, IVs and key reuse
procedure: Trace recovered constants to actual key/IV use; do not classify public keys, sample data or algorithm names as exposed secrets.

title: Weak algorithms, modes and static IVs
procedure: Validate DES/RC4/ECB, weak hashes and static IV usage in a security-sensitive context. RSA/ECB transformation naming is not symmetric ECB encryption.

title: Security-sensitive random generation
procedure: Trace token/key/nonce generation to a CSPRNG. A java.util.Random or Dart Random reference alone does not establish security-sensitive use.

title: Key lifecycle and platform protection
procedure: Verify Android Keystore provider, access policy, invalidation and exportability; record hardware backing only when attested.

title: Every application bridge boundary
procedure: Audit all discovered native/JNI/Flutter/RN/Cordova/.NET bridge implementations and their caller/argument validation.

title: Exported components and content providers
procedure: Invoke approved components with controlled inputs and verify authorization/read/write guards. An exported launcher is not inherently vulnerable.

title: Deep links, App Links and routing
procedure: Compare manifest intent filters with verified link ownership, navigation and authentication requirements; test controlled redirect/injection cases.

title: WebView navigation, JS bridges and content policy
procedure: Test allowed navigation, JavaScript bridge exposure, file access and mixed content with approved controlled content.

title: Intent and inter-app information exposure
procedure: Trace explicit/implicit intents, grants and extras; use an approved receiving test app to confirm any disclosure.

title: Permission necessity and use
procedure: Compare declared/granted permissions against documented functions and observed use; do not auto-classify every dangerous permission as a finding.

title: Root detection and server-sensitive decisions
procedure: Compare approved rooted/non-rooted environments and sensitive server actions against the documented threat model.

title: Emulator detection and expected behavior
procedure: Compare emulator/device behavior and documented policy; launching successfully in Genymotion alone is not a vulnerability.

title: Debugger detection and enforcement
procedure: Test approved debugger attachment and compare actual security-sensitive behavior; debuggable=false is not an anti-debugging test.

title: Frida/Xposed and instrumentation resistance
procedure: Compare baseline and approved instrumentation techniques; attachment alone cannot establish complete RASP effectiveness.

title: Signature verification and repackaging detection
procedure: Re-sign a controlled copy and verify client/server integrity decisions, preserving both artifact hashes and signing identities.

title: Compiled-code patch and hook resistance
procedure: Test approved patches to the actual Dart/native/Hermes/managed layer and document detection, compatibility and limitations.

title: Behavior after integrity compromise
procedure: Verify the agreed restrict/block/warn response and server-side handling of sensitive actions. Expected behavior comes from the app threat model.

title: Server-side transfer limits
procedure: Use seeded balances and documented limits; test boundary amounts and verify server-ledger outcomes and rollback.

title: Beneficiary ownership and authorization
procedure: Compare two controlled owners for beneficiary addition/deletion and step-up checks. Use mobile_identity_set + mobile_authz_sweep to confirm deterministically that cross-owner beneficiary add/delete is rejected.

title: Transaction replay and idempotency
procedure: Resubmit one approved test transaction and confirm ledger/idempotency effects without real fund movement. Use mobile_txn_probe with the request's idempotency field (plus amount/limit/currency invariants) to resubmit deterministically; it flags only when the server accepts a duplicate or invariant-breaking request, and distinguishes a correctly idempotent already-processed response. For concurrency/TOCTOU (double-spend, limit bypass, coupon stacking), run mobile_race_probe to fire K identical copies in parallel; a finding only when more acceptances than legitimate occur. Verify ledger integrity out-of-band with mobile_balance_check: read the balance, perform the transaction, read it again — an accepted transfer must debit exactly the amount, and a rejected one must leave the balance unchanged.

title: Concurrent balance and transaction enforcement
procedure: Use explicitly approved low-concurrency races and seeded accounts; verify ledger consistency and recovery.

title: Account, statement, beneficiary and application IDOR
procedure: Use owned test objects across accounts and roles; confirm access and mutations are rejected where required. Drive this with mobile_authz_sweep / mobile_authz_diff over the owned objects (identities from mobile_identity_set); a 2xx alone is not proof — require disclosure or unauthorized-mutation evidence.

title: Negative, fractional and overflow amounts
procedure: Evaluate documented amount bounds and precision with seeded transactions; check server and ledger results.

title: Currency and locale manipulation
procedure: Test declared currency/rate/locale invariants and server normalization with non-production accounts.

title: KYC file type, paths and document authorization
procedure: Upload approved harmless fixtures; verify file validation, path handling and cross-user document access.

title: Card block, limits and PIN authorization
procedure: Use issuer-provided test cards and documented role/step-up rules for each card operation.

title: Statement/PDF injection and access control
procedure: Generate seeded statements and compare owner/role access; use harmless validation markers in approved fields.

title: Release flags and debug/test endpoints
procedure: Verify release provenance, debuggable/testOnly, debug banners and reachable development endpoints; test endpoint reachability only in scope.

title: Release backup and transfer policy
procedure: Review the declared backup setting together with extraction rules and actual supported-OS behavior.

title: Build-time obfuscation evidence
procedure: Review verified build outputs and symbol/mapping handling for each detected language/runtime; APK inspection alone cannot confirm all compiler flags.

title: Exposed development/VM service interfaces
procedure: Inspect known development artifacts and approved runtime listeners; static strings or an idle run cannot establish that no service is exposed.

title: Production analytics and crash confidentiality
procedure: Verify production telemetry configuration and captured seeded events across SDKs and code layers.

title: Finding MASVS v2 and CWE mapping
procedure: Assign verified control IDs and CWE where relevant; pre-engagement and backend-only controls may require separate ASVS/API mappings rather than a fabricated MASVS equivalence.

title: Repeatable evidence and tool/patch provenance
procedure: Include original/modified hashes, device/OS, tool versions, commands, raw exchanges and actual results. Do not invent execution evidence.

title: Severity, financial impact and regulatory context
procedure: Explain CVSS and business impact using validated financial/PII exposure and the agreed regulatory context; no automatic compliance certification.

title: Remediation ownership and layer separation
procedure: Assign app/business code, native/platform integration and backend API owners; deduplicate cross-layer causes and record retest status.

title: PendingIntent mutability and broadcast safety
procedure: Review PendingIntent creation: confirm FLAG_IMMUTABLE is set (or the wrapped Intent is explicit when mutability is genuinely required), and that implicit broadcasts carry no sensitive extras (use setPackage for intra-app messaging).

title: Content provider SQL injection and path traversal
procedure: Review ContentProvider query/insert/update/delete/openFile and FileProvider file_paths.xml. Confirm parameterized SQL (no string concatenation) and that openFile canonicalizes paths within the sandbox; reject ../ traversal and overly broad root-path/external-path declarations.

title: Tapjacking and overlay protection
procedure: Confirm sensitive views set setFilterTouchesWhenObscured(true)/android:filterTouchesWhenObscured and that authentication/transaction screens resist overlay tapjacking; test with an approved overlay app.

title: Native binary memory mitigations
procedure: Inspect ELF headers of lib/<abi>/*.so for Position Independent Executable (PIE), full RELRO, non-executable stack (NX), stack canaries and stripped symbol tables (e.g. checksec/readelf).

title: App integrity and server-side attestation
procedure: Check runtime signing-certificate self-verification and Google Play Integrity API (or hardware key attestation): confirm integrity tokens use a server-generated nonce and are verified on the backend, never solely on-device.
